what: Mission-based alarm apps (Erly / Early / push-up alarm): AI-verified physical tasks (push-ups etc.) to turn off alarm. Hit ~$50k/mo in 4 months, 200k+ downloads. Alarmy (older player) does hundreds of k$/mo with missions.
why_us: Proven simple consumer pain (snoozing) with high willingness to pay via sub. Viral TikTok/IG hook + AI verification. Low complexity, high retention via streaks. Multiple clones succeeding.
engagement: High virality, 16k App Store reviews 4.8*, case studies circulating

what: Postiz — open-source agentic social media scheduler. Repositioned for AI agents, open-source distribution + viral agent content → $145k–$176k MRR, approaching $2M+ ARR as solo founder.
why_us: Shows power of open-source + AI-agent positioning. Clear distribution playbook (GitHub stars → cloud conversions, agent wave). High repeatability for similar agent tools.
engagement: Hundreds of likes on updates, 15k+ followers, daily MRR posts

what: Artist-specific community platform like old DeviantArt but actively moderated against AI-generated content. DA is 'dead', artists want pure human art community with filtering.
why_us: Massive engagement (6k likes, 500+ RTs on key post). Clear underserved niche: professional + hobbyist artists fleeing AI-flooded platforms. Monetization via pro features, commissions, premium no-AI feeds.

what: Wrestle AI — combat sports AI app. 100k+ downloads, $400k ARR in first 9 months via influencer marketing only, 68% margins, almost no paid ads.
why_us: Niche vertical AI (wrestling) with proven influencer-led growth. Shows power of single-channel mastery below $10k MRR. High margins, seasonal upside.

what: AI businesses monetizing characters/short-form: one example grew from $870 to $15.7k in 30 days (mostly messaging + subs). Character as asset, content acquires attention, sub opens relationship.
why_us: Concrete 18x growth case. Pattern for AI character/UGC wrappers: attention → profile → sub → messaging upsell. Low production cost via AI.

what: Free / open-source alternatives directory demand remains strong. One post claiming 'biggest free alternative directory' (1832 alts to 422 apps) got strong engagement. SaaS subscription fatigue continues.
why_us: Recurring pain: rising SaaS costs, feature bloat, lock-in. Directories and lightweight open-source replacements keep winning attention.
